# Survey of existing Lean

This is the scout report from [issue #3](https://github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo/issues/3), copied here so that agents working without network access can read it. It lists declarations in Mathlib and in other Lean projects that cover parts of the paper, with pinned commits. None of this code is vendored; see [`README.md`](README.md) for the convention.

---

# Scout 1 · Lean precedents for Masullo’s number-field argument

All 87 numbered sections in the contents (Chapters 1–14 and Appendices A–E) were scouted. The entries below and the five linked surveys distinguish results checked on the project pin, upstream proofs inspected at a fixed commit, partial matches, and unsuccessful searches for the stated generality.

| Where to look | Highest-value result or obstacle |
|---|---|
| [Chapters 2–3, 14 and Appendices A–B](https://github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo/issues/3#issuecomment-7048797926) | Adelic Schwartz–Bruhat functions, theta, Tate continuation and functional equation. Translated lattice counts, Dedekind explicit formula, a comparator-checked unitary Hecke zero-free region for Re(s) > 7/8, and remaining coefficient/normalization comparisons. |
| [Chapters 4, 7, 9–10 and Appendices C–D](https://github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo/issues/3#issuecomment-7048798228) | Smooth Fourier series and periodization, nuclear Schwartz spaces, Mellin inversion, Peter–Weyl and Euclidean kernel theorems. The precise topology and the choice of basis matter. |
| [Chapters 5, 6, 8 and Appendix E](https://github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo/issues/3#issuecomment-7048798556) | Stackification, action groupoids, compact generation and weak Hausdorffness. The transporter uniqueness in Prop. 8.2.0.4 fails for the printed full idele group. Thm. 8.3.0.1(1) uses it on p. 388. |
| [Chapter 1 overview and Chapters 11–12](https://github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo/issues/3#issuecomment-7048798918) | Physlib’s trace-class identities compile on our exact pin. Brislawn and Connes provide comparisons for the diagonal and finite-S calculations. The global shell identity remains unverified. |
| [Chapters 1 and 13, deduction about zeros](https://github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo/issues/3#issuecomment-7048799269) | The cutoff-independent bound on p. 29 fails already over ℚ at z = 2. Fatou’s lemma gives a logarithmic divergence. The prime sum also has a sign discrepancy. The final divisor statement on p. 522 is blank. |

**Search scope.** We compared sections and cited theorems with pinned Mathlib, live public Lean repositories, public code search, a local mirror of Lean projects and relevant non-Lean proofs. The mirror filename pass returned 37,927 candidate paths before duplicate and relevance filtering. Some large GitHub trees were truncated, so targeted searches and direct file lookups supplemented them. The detailed surveys link exact proof files, toolchains and audit limits. No exact public Lean proof of the paper’s global trace formula surfaced. The index is a discovery survey and leaves porting and equivalence obligations explicit.

For analytic continuation see the Hanke results below. |

Mathlib gives tempered distributions the pointwise topology. Masullo requires uniform convergence on bounded sets, so use the strong dual when stating topological results. |

Construct the paper’s quotient stack on its compactly generated weak Hausdorff site, with the specified topology. |

The former bounds ζ on ½ ≤ Re(s) < 3 for ∣Im(s)∣ ≥ 1. The latter covers Dirichlet characters on Re(s) ≥ 1 with the pole excluded. Neither gives zero locations in the critical strip. |

**Verification.** All source links pin the inspected commits. The cited external projects are Apache-2.0. Our Mathlib uses Lean 4.36.0. Hanke, Imperial FLT, PrimeNumberTheoremAnd and Stacks use 4.35.0, Anthropic uses 4.33.1, and TauCeti uses 4.37.0-rc1. The Mathlib declarations elaborated locally in `.agent/Check.lean`. Local axiom checks for real Poisson summation, Dirichlet nonvanishing, Anthropic’s adelic span induction and its Fourier-integral comparison showed only the three permitted axioms. Hanke’s [successful Tate comparator](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/actions/runs/44516056745/job/135543910258) checks all five headline theorems against [this explicit axiom allowlist](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/comparator/Tate.json). For the other cited external results I inspected source with proof bodies and found no direct `sorry` in the cited declarations. Their transitive axioms and portability remain unchecked locally.

**Trace formula and missing deduction.** Masullo cites [Connes, §VII, Theorem 4, p. 31](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9811068#page=31) on p. 519 for the finite-set-of-places calculation. I found no checked Lean counterpart of Masullo’s global Theorem 12.5.1.1. On p. 522 the printed Theorem 13.3.1.1 counts critical-line zeros with multiplicities capped at the field degree. The transition to Theorem 13.3.1.2 cites “Theorem ??” and leaves the divisor statement blank. The draft therefore supplies no finished deduction at that location to translate into Lean.

**Appendix matches found on a second pass.** Both linked modules below are from Hanke’s Apache-2.0 repository on Lean 4.35.0. I inspected the proofs at the linked revision. I have not compiled these modules against this project’s pin.

| Appendix item | Formal precedent | Remaining comparison |
|---|---|---|
| A.4.1.1, pp. 562–563 | `NumberFieldKB.WeilBNT.span_gammaLattice` and `NumberFieldKB.WeilBNT.finrank_gammaLattice` identify the span of the logarithmic S-unit lattice and give rank ∣S∣−1. [SUnits.lean](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/WeilBNT/SUnits.lean) | Reuse this for the arithmetic input. A.4.1.1 further bounds the number of S-units in a box translated by an idele, uniformly as its norm goes to zero. |
| D.1.2.7, p. 749 | `NumberFieldKB.Pontryagin.poisson_summation` gives equality of the sum on a discrete cocompact subgroup and the Fourier sum on its annihilator, with a covolume-one normalization and admissibility hypotheses. [Poisson.lean](https://github.com/jonhanke/algebraic-number-theory-lean/blob/5ea368e03a066197d53114efa8be66d351a9f060/NumberFieldKB/Pontryagin/Poisson.lean) | Use it for lattice applications after checking admissibility. D.1.2.7 allows any closed subgroup and includes an almost-everywhere identity under integrability assumptions. |
| B.4.4.7 and C.3.7.1 | The former states the idelic explicit formula for every number field. The latter invokes Brislawn, Cor. 3.2, p. 237 and Thm. 3.1, p. 235, for the trace of an integral kernel (as cited by Masullo). | I have not verified an exact Lean counterpart for either. In B.4, p. 625, footnote 27 explicitly requests an explanation of how one identity follows from B.4.2.2. In C.3.7.1 the theorem must also specify the representative or smoothing used to evaluate an L² kernel on the diagonal. |
